newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Macmin says PNG mine confirms gold hopes.
newsitem.headline: Macmin says PNG mine confirms gold hopes.

text.p: Junior miner Macmin NL said on Tuesday a series of high-grade gold results confirmed initial estimates of a 200,000-ounce resource at its Imwauna Prospect on Papua New Guinea's Normanby Island.

The Queensland-based miner said in a statement "consistent and continuous" high-grade gold had been documented by deep trench sampling over a previously drilled 950-metre section of an epithermal quartz vein system.

It said one trench recorded 0.6 metres at 223 grams per tonne (g/t) gold, while weighted assay averages of the vein and adjacent walll rock produced results which included 2.84 metres at 13.5 g/t and 2.85 metres at 11.79 g/t.
Quartz material intersected in 49 trenches sampled to date averaged 12.6 g/t over an average width of 0.64 metres.
Diluted to one metre, the average grade of the 1,250 m vein length is 7.9 g/t, Macmin said.

Macmin managing director Bob McNeil said the high grade of the results indicated the project's economic promise, with potential existing to add to the existing resource of 990,000 tonnes at 6.1 g/t gold and 12 g/t silver.
"The Imwauna Vein Swarm covers an area of 3.5 kms by 1.3 kms and includes numerous veins in addition to the section trenched so far," McNeil said.

"There is clear potential for a major open pittable resource based both on narrow high-grade veins and low-grade disseminated mineralisation, such as that identified at the Imwauna-Knob area," he said.
